title: SlideCast Studio v4.0 “DECAL”
subtitle: Update — on-slide stickers, progressive reveals, entrance and exit effects
description: v4.0 “DECAL” lets you add text and images over finished slides, then control their timing, entrance, exit and sound effects.
author: aokuma
hero_alt: SlideCast Studio v4.0 DECAL title image
source_note: The original note post is in Japanese and may include later additions or comments.

blocks.html:
SlideCast Studio has been updated to v4.0 “DECAL”.

The centrepiece is on-slide stickers: text and images that you can add over a finished slide. Without rebuilding the source slide, you can show labels, notes and images at the right point in an explanation, or cover information until you are ready to reveal it.

sections.title: Add explanations and images after a slide is finished
sections.intro: Add text and image stickers without leaving the video editor.

blocks.html:
Previously, adding a note or emphasis meant returning to the original PowerPoint or image, editing it and importing it again. In v4.0, the editor’s Sticker tab lets you add text stickers and image stickers.

Each slide can hold up to ten stickers. Move them directly in the preview, then use the corner and side handles to adjust their size, width and height.

blocks.caption: Text and images can be combined on the same slide

blocks.html: Placement can be switched between moving with the slide image and staying fixed to the whole canvas. The first option follows slide-image scaling and Ken Burns motion; the second fixes the sticker to the full frame, including areas outside the slide image.

blocks.alt: Controls for choosing the sticker placement reference

sections.title: Hide information, then reveal it one item at a time
sections.intro: Set start and end times to give a static slide a timed sequence.

blocks.html:
Every sticker can have its own display start and end time. Move its band on the timeline, or drag either end to change how long it remains visible.

A particularly useful technique is to cover information from the start, then remove the covering stickers one by one as the explanation progresses. You can reveal bullet points or quiz answers on a single static slide instead of duplicating it several times.

blocks.alt: A sticker sequence revealing bullet points one at a time
blocks.caption: Reveal a static slide progressively in time with the narration

items: Show a quiz answer after a few seconds
Reveal a comparison result after explaining the choices
Uncover a procedure one step at a time
Hide part of a photograph or diagram until it is discussed

blocks.html: Entrance and exit choices include none, fade, pop or shrink, slide in or out, wipe from the left, and float in from below or move away upwards. Each effect has fast, normal and slow speeds.

blocks.alt: Entrance and exit effect settings for a sticker
blocks.caption: Choose an entrance, exit and speed for each sticker

blocks.alt: The full timeline used to adjust sticker display timing
blocks.caption: Sticker timing can also be adjusted from the full timeline

blocks.title: 🖼️ Still-image, PDF and PPTX export
blocks.text: Formats without a time axis draw stickers in their state after effects have completed. You can also choose whether stickers are included.

sections.title: Play a sound when a sticker enters or exits
sections.intro: Pair visible changes with sound to guide the viewer’s attention.

blocks.html: A sticker can use a different sound for its entrance and exit. Seven sounds are built in:

You can also import your own MP3 and reuse it from the sticker sound-effect library. Put an exit sound on a sticker covering a bullet point, and the sound plays at the instant the item underneath appears.

sections.title: Align stickers neatly and reuse them from a library
sections.intro: Snap position, size and timing, and save frequently used assets and styles.

blocks.html: As you move a sticker, it snaps to the edges and centres of other stickers, as well as the centre of the canvas. While resizing, it can match another sticker’s width or height.

blocks.alt: Sticker position and size snapping into alignment

blocks.html: On the timeline, stickers snap to narration, other stickers’ start and end points, slide boundaries and the current playhead.

blocks.alt: A sticker time range snapping to audio and the playhead

blocks.html: Save frequently used images to the Sticker Image Library, and configured stickers — including appearance, size and sound effects — to the Sticker Library. Position and display timing are deliberately not saved, so each sticker is easier to fit to a new slide.

blocks.alt: Saving a configured sticker to the Sticker Library
blocks.caption: A library item can be reused on other slides

sections.title: Mosaic and blur masks are now available
sections.intro: A text sticker can also act as a panel that hides part of a slide.

blocks.html: Choose mosaic or blur and set its strength from 1 to 100. Leave the text empty to use the sticker only as a mask. You can also make just the background colour translucent for decorative uses.

blocks.alt: Mosaic and blur controls for a sticker

blocks.title: ⚠️ Hiding personal or confidential information
blocks.text: A weak mosaic or blur may leave the original content guessable. Use a strong setting or cover it with a fully opaque solid colour.

sections.title: The settings and script area has been reorganised
sections.intro: Choose the tab for the task at hand and go directly to the controls you need.

blocks.html: Normal mode now has five tabs — Script, Timeline, Slide Settings, Stickers and Auto-acting. Easy mode has three — Script, Stickers and Auto-acting. Showing only the selected group also reduces vertical scrolling.

blocks.alt: The Script, Timeline, Slide Settings, Stickers and Auto-acting tabs

items: Frequently checked controls such as content, position and timing remain visible
Details such as colour, borders and shadows are grouped into collapsible sections or popovers
Collapsed sections still summarise their current settings
Buttons, inputs, cards and selected states now share a consistent appearance

sections.title: More control over lettering and shadows
sections.intro: Letter spacing and shadow controls now cover subtitles, captions, badges and stickers.

blocks.html:
You can adjust letter spacing for subtitles, per-character subtitles, badges, captions and text stickers. Open it slightly for atmosphere, or tighten a long caption to fit.

Shadow controls are now organised around colour, type, opacity, blur and distance, and are easier to use across character icons, speech bubbles, subtitles, captions, badges and stickers.

blocks.alt: Controls for adjusting a text shadow

sections.title: Bug fixes and stability improvements
sections.intro: Memory and processing have been reviewed for long projects and large images.

items: Limit images held during full playback and video export to those currently needed
Reduce unnecessary screen updates during playback and autosaves during continuous operations
Fix an overly long seek bar on slides without audio
Improve the stability of video-background previews
Fix a crash caused by resetting certain settings
Fix sticker selection handles shifting after leaving Timing Focus mode

sections.title: Existing projects and storage limits
sections.intro: Existing visuals and audio do not change on their own. Keep an eye on asset count and memory use.

blocks.html:
Existing projects with no stickers continue to display without stickers. New sound effects and redaction masks are off by default.

Images, animated images and sound effects are stored in the browser, so they use storage according to their number and size.

blocks.title: ⚠️ Animated images
blocks.text: Even a small file can use substantial memory during playback if it has many frames or large dimensions. If performance suffers, try a smaller image or a shorter animation.

sections.title: How to update to v4.0
sections.intro: If you have already purchased SlideCast Studio, copy v4.0 from the same shared link in the paid note post.

blocks.title: 💾 Make a backup first
blocks.text: If you want to carry over projects, libraries and settings, create a backup from Data Storage before updating.

blocks.html: To update the Apps Script edition without changing its URL, replace “無題.html” and “AppBundle.html” in the existing Apps Script project with the files from the v4.0 distribution folder, then redeploy the existing deployment as a new version.

blocks.label: Detailed update instructions for the Apps Script edition

blocks.html: For the local HTML edition, download and open “SlideCast Studio v4.0【ローカル版】.html”. Data from the previous edition will not appear automatically in a new Apps Script project or a different browser, so restore it from your backup.

sections.title: Design not only a slide, but the order in which it is seen
sections.intro: What to add, where to put it, when to show it, how it arrives and leaves, and what sound goes with it.

blocks.html:
With v4.0, every slide can now define what to add, where to put it, when to show it, how it appears and disappears, and what sound accompanies it.

Use it to make explainers, product introductions, lessons, dialogue videos and short-form videos clearer and easier to follow whenever presentation order matters.
